entries.title: Numbers 24:1
segments:
Enchantments; this word seems to describe the superstitious means which Balaam employed to obtain revelations from God. 
 
  Wilderness; where the Israelites camped. 
 
The Lord will cause all men to see htat it is his unchangeable purpose to bless his people.  Those who rejoice in it will be partakers of his joy, and those who are grieved at it be filled with ever-growing sorrow.

entries.title: Numbers 24:3
segments: Whose eyes are open; the eyes of whose mind are opened to see God's revelation.

entries.title: Numbers 24:4
segments: However much men may know of God and his ways, and however much they may see of the blessedness of his people, if they do not love and obey him, their knowledge will but increase their guilt and aggravate their ruin.

entries.title: Numbers 24:6
segments: Lign-aloes; an oriental tree remarkable for the fragrance of its wood.

entries.title: Numbers 24:7
segments:
He shall pour the water out of his buckets; or, "water shall flow from his buckets," that is, in a full stream.  Water is here an emblem of the divine blessing which shall make Israel strong and numerous. 
 
  In many waters; or, by many waters,
.  His posterity shall flourish like trees planted by many waters.

entries.title: Numbers 24:8
segments: Eat up the nations; overcome and destroy them.

entries.title: Numbers 24:9
segments: God will treat men in some measure as they treat his people.  The blessings which they bestow, or the curses which they heap upon them; will return upon themselves.

entries.title: Numbers 24:11
segments: By refusing to please the wicked, men often fail of those worldly honors which by doing wrong they might obtain.

entries.title: Numbers 24:13
segments: Men may feel their dependence on God, that they are under his control and cannot escape out of his hands, without rejoicing in their dependence, receiving mercies with gratitude, or giving him the glory of what they enjoy.

entries.title: Numbers 24:15
segments: Whose eyes are open; to see and foretell many things that will hereafter take place.

entries.title: Numbers 24:17
segments: See him--behold him; the Star and the Sceptre that shall rise out of Israel.  The reference is undoubtedly to the Messiah, but in such a way that it includes David's kingdom also, which was perpetuated and received a spiritual form in Christ.

David's victories over the Moabites and other enemies of Israel were but anticipations and pledges of the final victory which Jesus Christ, his son according to the flesh and sitting upon his throne, should gain over all the enemies of His people.
The children of Sheth; or, as many prefer, the children of tumult, the tumultuous warriors of Moab.

entries.title: Numbers 24:21
segments: The Kenites; apparently a Midianitish people dwelling in near connection with the Amalekites.

entries.title: Numbers 24:23
segments:
Who shall live? who can escape destruction in the midst of such desolations? 
 
A view of the future, while it awakens gladness in the righteous, fills the wicked with apprehension and dismay.

entries.title: Numbers 24:24
segments:
Ships; armed forces coming in ships. 
 
  The coast of Chittim; the countries of the west lying on the Mediterranean.  This prophecy was fulfilled in the conquests of the Greeks and Romans over the East. 
 
  Eber; the posterity of Eber living on the east of the Euphrates. To this people and region Abraham belonged, and thence he migrated to the land of Canaan.  To this country Balaam also belonged, so that he who was called to curse Israel was compelled to foretell the doom of "the children of his people." 
 
  He also; probably, the power that comes from Chittim, but some understand the words of Eber.  Balaam having thus far foretold the perpetual triumph of God's people and the overthrow of all their enemies, ceases and departs.
